newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA SAYS WORRIED AT REGIONAL TRADE IMBALANCE.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA SAYS WORRIED AT REGIONAL TRADE IMBALANCE.

text.p: South African Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin said on Friday urgent steps were needed to reduce the trade imbalance between South Africa and its southern African neighbours.
"We have pretty severe problems emerging in SADC (Southern African Development Community). The trade balance in our favour is growing very dramatically," Erwin told a conference.
He said in 1996 South Africa's trade surplus with its neighbours stood at 10 billion rand. The trade balance in South Africa's favour with Zimbabwe alone grew by one billion rand last year, he added.

"Changes are very, very fast and very dramatic and they are going to have a powerful adverse effect on our neighbouring economies unless we take urgent steps either through investment flows and/or through trade flows with our neighbours."
Development of the SADC was vital to South Africa, he said.

"I think this is one of the fundamentals of our economic policy that if we do not bring about a development process in SADC, then it is highly unlikely that South Africa's own growth process can succeed," he said.

"For us in trade and industry the priority negotiations at the moment by far are the SADC negotiations, and in many respects the structure of that agreement precedes conceptually and actually any agreement we may reach with the European Union," he added.

SADC includes Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe and represents 40 percent of Africa's population and 80 percent of the continent's GDP.
South Africa is the biggest investor in southern Africa and in 1991 had invested nine billion rand in the region, figures show.
